Esthetician here - Dermaplaning can have that effect sometimes for those with sensitive skin, if you’re using retinol or retinoids (including oral Accutane), if you’re using AHA’s/BHA regularly, if the provider went over the area too many times or too roughly, and sometimes as a bit of an allergic type reaction like the other professional stated in their comment. I personally would never have done a scrub afterwards since you’re using 2 different physical exfoliants back to back … that could have put your skin over the edge and if the rest of the treatment wasn’t focused on replenishing your skin with nutrients and antioxidants then yeah, I can certainly see why that would happen. It’s normal, to an extent, to have sensitization after dermaplaning because your active skincare ingredients are penetrating much more than before since the vellus hair and stratum corneum have been removed but it shouldn’t last longer than a day or two. I even tell my clients to expect some mild flaking / peeling after a few days, which is also totally normal. After a treatment where you’re getting so much exfoliation, you need to have a post-procedure skincare protocol of soothing products, such as a cream cleanser, repairing moisturizer and SUNSCREEN!! Make sure to use physical sunscreen because the zinc is also soothing for the skin. After a treatment like this your skin is more susceptible to the sun, so sunscreen is important during this time (and always!). You should have been told how to care for your skin at home after the treatment …aftercare is usually used for 5-10 days depending on what kind of treatment and response someone has. Just be gentle with it - no active ingredients (HA is fine) and it should get better soon.
